items.gist: When a teacher wishes to install a disciple as putraka, sādhaka, or guru, he first performs adhivāsa and on the second day draws the maṇḍala.
Three triśūlas are drawn with three devīs placed in middle, left, and right positions, completing full worship.
Seven gurus from Gaṇapati to Kṣetrapati are worshipped in the eastern direction before the maṇḍala.
The paśu is offered through advaya-bhāvanā, dissolving its elements into the devatā-cakra for Śiva's satisfaction.
The paśu is dissolved via prāṇa-manipulation, kuṇḍalinī, and kalā-melting, culminating in śiva-yojana.
Six adhvans are placed on the disciple's body with measured spans from feet to crown.
Seventy śodhaka mantras and ten śodhya types yield 1021 dīkṣā varieties by combination.
Dīkṣā divides into bhoga (with sub-varieties) and mokṣa, the latter single yet differentiated by disciple capacity.
Mantra-śakti is parāmarśa; the guru's vimarśa becomes śiva-tā through mantra-abhyāsa.
Without dīkṣā no adhikāra in yoga; dīkṣā purifies karma and leads to laya in Śiva.
